transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood CSM), Eric Huang (Redwood SE); Dana Li, Ravi Singh, Maya Torres (Monarch Retail)

Summary: Quarterly business review covering usage, cost anomalies, three reliability incidents in last 60 days, and roadmap alignment for Dedicated capacity pilot.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes, we'll do a quick run of health metrics and then talk next steps, lina you wanna kick off?
[00:12] Lina: yeah thanks Samir; hi Dana, Ravi, Maya — happy qbr, quick note, transcription may be a bit rough on some infra terms, so apologies if K V cache becomes K V cash, etc.
[00:25] Dana: yeah that's fine, thanks. jumping in — overall things are good, but we've seen a spike in token consumption in May tied to a new autocomplete feature. cost climbed about 28% month over month.
[00:40] Eric: can you share the rough numbers? tokens, calls per second, seq lengths?
[00:45] Dana: sure so average request tokens went from 120 to about 210, peak RPS hasn't changed much, still around 18 rps, but longer sequences from context-aware recs and convo state. total monthly tokens jumped from ~1.1B to 1.4B.
[01:05] Samir: thanks that's helpful. we've got a couple levers: batching, prefix caching, and a different quantization / model variant to reduce cost. for production predictability you mentioned considering Dedicated—where are you on timeline?
[01:22] Maya: we're evaluating Dedicated for predictable latency and audit controls. procurement wants a timeline this quarter if possible.
[01:30] Ravi: also worth noting we have strict data residency needs for EU traffic and want KMS integration for keys.
[01:38] Lina: we can support EU region with Private / Dedicated routing and KMS — i'll share the detailed security pack after the call.
[01:45] Dana: great. on reliability I flagged three incidents in last 60 days, two were transient OOM on longer sequences, one was a cache invalidation bug from our side but we saw increased tail latency for about 20 minutes.
[01:58] Eric: on the OOMs we saw those logs — looks like sequence length distribution exceeded the default compilation kernel. we recommended switching to a longer-context kernel and enabling streaming for those flows. did you try streaming?
[02:10] Ravi: we did not, we were concerned about client changes. but we can try minimal streaming changes.
[02:15] Samir: small streaming changes often reduce tail latency because tokens are pipelined, and enables earlier responses for pagination style UIs. also we can set a per-route sequence cap to avoid kernel bloat.
[02:30] Dana: sounds good — but cost is still a concern. can you quantify cost delta if we enable prefix caching + batching?
[02:38] Eric: rough back-of-envelope: with caching of repeated prefixes and a batch size tuned to 4-6 you could see 20-35% token-cost reduction for those heavy flows. exact savings depend on hit rate; we'll need to run a bench on your traffic patterns.
[02:52] Maya: and does enabling caching impact privacy / data retention? legal will ask.
[02:56] Lina: caching is optional and can be scoped per-route; cached prefixes are encrypted at rest and we can honor retention windows, and KMS handles key access controls. i'll include that in the security doc.
[03:10] Samir: to the procurement point — dedicated pricing is a committed capacity model; we sent a starter quote last quarter, but we can propose a burst + baseline commit that fits your 24/7 baseline and spiky marketing loads.
[03:24] Dana: do you have any SLA numbers we can include in procurement packet?
[03:28] Samir: yes we provide SLOs for p95 latency and uptime for Dedicated; i'll add the SLA appendix to the pricing doc.
[03:35] Ravi: on the private deployment — for EU traffic we'd rather have VPC with private control plane. is that supported?
[03:42] Eric: yes, Private VPC is supported; there's an on-prem option too but that's heavier. for most customers VPC + customer-managed KMS meets compliance needs.
[03:52] Maya: okay good. also curious about rollouts — we want canary + automatic fallback if a model variant regresses. is that something Redwood supports today?
[04:02] Samir: yes, rollouts with canary, A/B, and automatic fallback exist. we can tie quality monitors to your eval sets so a regression triggers rollback.
[04:12] Dana: perfect. for the benchmark we want to compare hosted vs dedicated under our 75th/95th percentile loads with long context (up to 1,200 tokens). is that feasible?
[04:22] Eric: absolutely. we'll need a tokenized sample trace and clear success criteria — latency at p95 under X ms and cost per million tokens under Y.
[04:32] Ravi: i'll export traces and share a sanitized trace this week.
[04:36] Samir: great — next steps summarized at the end.
[04:40] [INTERMISSION - 4m, quick screen share of dashboard metrics] 
[09:00] Lina: walking through usage dashboard — note the spike on May 18 correlates with rollout of the new autocomplete. the top-consuming route is /recommend/v2.
[09:18] Dana: that's right — we had a bug that increased context retention for 2 hours that day. we've fixed it.
[09:25] Eric: on reliability incidents: two were infra-level memory pressure, we recommended increasing the KV cache allocation and switching to an alternate compilation kernel during the heavy batch window. any change in your config recently?
[09:40] Ravi: we increased max_seq for an internal test but forgot to revert, that likely caused the OOMs.
[09:46] Samir: good catch — that aligns. small config drift is common; we can provide a config audit checklist to avoid regression.
[09:55] Maya: one ask — can we get token-level cost breakdown by route for the last 90 days?
[10:01] Lina: yes we'll export per-route cost; it will show tokens, calls, p95 latency, and nominal cost. expect it by EOD tomorrow.
[10:09] Dana: thank you.
[10:12] Samir: on Dedicated sizing: we propose baseline 4x A100 equivalent for your 24/7 flows with burst pool for marketing peaks; this is preliminary. we'd like to run a pilot for 4 weeks.
[10:25] Maya: procurement will want ROI — can you model projected savings vs hosted if we adopt caching + quantized model + Dedicated?
[10:33] Samir: yes we can model that; we'll provide a conservative and optimistic scenario.
[10:37] Ravi: about KMS — how does key rotation work during rollout? we can't have downtime.
[10:42] Eric: KMS rotates keys with zero-downtime semantics; we use envelope encryption and the runtime caches DEKs for active sessions, rotation is seamless. we'll document the flow.
[10:55] [15:00] Maya: on road map — any upcoming features that help us reduce tail latency?
[15:05] Eric: we're shipping a per-route kernel selector that will reduce kernel miscompilation at runtime and a smarter batching scheduler that respects latency SLOs. both are in Canary late Q3.
[15:18] Dana: excellent. are there required client changes for the new scheduler?
[15:22] Eric: no client changes — it's on the serving layer. streaming improvements might require minor client adaptions.
[15:30] Samir: okay quick recap and commitments: 1) Samir send updated Dedicated pricing + SLA appendix by 6/27; 2) Lina share SOC2/security docs and KMS integration notes by 6/26; 3) Eric + Ravi run benchmark (hosted vs dedicated) week of 7/6 and share results by 7/10; 4) export per-route cost report by Lina by EOD tomorrow.
[15:54] Maya: sounds good to me.
[15:57] Dana: agreed.
[16:00] Ravi: we'll prepare trace and reach out to Eric to set up the benchmark.
[16:05] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and schedule the pilot kickoff once pricing is agreed.
[16:12] [END]
